question.text: Which of the following is MOST accurately characterised as a default for which SEBI may initiate adjudication under the SEBI Act 1992 against a SIAO (Social Impact Assessment Organization, i.e., an intermediary employing SIAs)?

answer.text: Failure to prepare pro-bono work for a registered charity.
Failure to deliver a public keynote at an industry conference.
Failure to advertise the SIAO's services online.
Failure to furnish statutory returns / information to SEBI, failure to enter into written client agreements, failure to comply with specified conditions of registration.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook summarises Section 9.3: SEBI may impose penalties / adjudicate against intermediaries on grounds such as failure to furnish information / return / report, failure to enter into an agreement with clients, and other specified defaults. These are the statutory trigger events. The Trap: Pro-bono work, advertising and public keynotes are not regulatory duties - they are business choices without SEBI-Act sanction. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C and XXIV AML both test SEBI Act grounds; XXIII applies them to SIAOs. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Maintain a rolling SEBI-returns calendar with two-week pre-deadline reminders. A single missed annual return has triggered SAT-reviewable adjudication orders in real cases - prevention is trivially cheap.
